description.summary: embed a client's surface into a window of the host application

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a client embed its surface into a window of a host application, which runs the compositor that the client is connected to.
For example, an audio application runs a Wayland compositor of its own, which forwards the requests of its clients to the system compositor, and its plugins embed their user interfaces into its windows. See the clap_plugin_gui_wayland_nested_compositor extension in include/clap/ext/draft/wayland-experiment.h.
The host application gives an embedding token to the client by other means than this protocol, for example with the CLAP plugin API. The client creates a wl_surface, and embeds it with get_embedded_surface and the token.
This protocol is experimental. It is based on the ext_surface_embedding_v1 draft by jwolffpsl: https://github.com/free-audio/clap/issues/474#issuecomment-4177525720

interface.name: clap_surface_embedding_v1

description.summary: embed surfaces into windows of the host application

interface.description: The compositor of the host application exposes this global.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has another role

entry.name: already_embedded
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a clap_embedded_surface_v1 object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this object. The embedded surfaces which it created remain.

request.name: get_embedded_surface
request.description:
Gives the wl_surface the embedded surface role, and embeds it at the place which the token designates.
The token is an opaque string, which the host application gave to the client by other means. If the compositor doesn't know the token, if another embedded surface already uses it, or if the compositor refuses the embedding for any other reason, it sends the closed event to the new object. Any client of the compositor could present a token, so the host application should make its tokens hard to guess.
It is a protocol error to give a wl_surface which already has another role, or which already has a clap_embedded_surface_v1 object. After its clap_embedded_surface_v1 object is destroyed, the wl_surface may be embedded again.

arg.name: token
arg.summary: embedding token from the host application

interface.name: clap_embedded_surface_v1

description.summary: a surface embedded into a window of the host application

interface.description:
An embedded surface appears inside a window of the host application, at the place which the host application chose. The compositor positions it; the client can't.
The surface is mapped when a buffer is attached and committed, and unmapped when a null buffer is committed. Its size is the size of its buffer, or of its viewport, and the host application and the client agree on it by other means than this protocol, for example with the CLAP plugin API. The compositor may clip the surface to the area which the host application reserved for it.
The compositor applies the surface's commits as soon as possible, as for a desynchronized wl_subsurface. It may synchronize them with the host application's own commits, for example while the area is resized, so that both appear at once.
The surface receives input events like any other surface. The compositor gives it the keyboard focus as it sees fit, for example when the user clicks into it.
For its popups, like menus and tooltips, and for its dialogs, the client uses the standard protocols on the same connection, with the parents which get_parent_surface and get_parent_toplevel give.
If the wl_surface is destroyed, this object becomes inert: the compositor ignores its requests, and the client should destroy it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Unmaps the surface, and destroys this object.

request.name: get_parent_surface

description.summary: get the parent surface, for popups

request.description:
Creates an xdg_surface object which refers to the host application's surface containing the embedded surface: the closest xdg_surface, a toplevel or a popup, among the embedded surface's ancestors. The client uses it as the parent of its popups, with xdg_surface.get_popup, and places them with the position event.
The new object only stands for the host application's surface. The compositor ignores all its requests except destroy, and sends no event on it. The client destroys it when it doesn't need it anymore.

request.name: get_parent_toplevel

description.summary: get the parent toplevel, for dialogs

request.description:
Creates an xdg_toplevel object which refers to the host application's toplevel containing the embedded surface. The client uses it as the parent of its own toplevels, for example its dialogs, with xdg_toplevel.set_parent.
The new object only stands for the host application's toplevel. The compositor ignores all its requests except destroy, and sends no event on it. The client destroys it when it doesn't need it anymore.

event.name: position
event.description:
The position of the embedded surface's top left corner, relative to the window geometry of the parent surface (see get_parent_surface), in the parent's surface-local coordinates. The client needs it to place its popups with xdg_positioner.
The compositor sends it right after get_embedded_surface, unless it sends closed, and whenever the position changes.

event.name: closed
event.description: The compositor ended the embedding, or refused it: for example the token was unknown or already in use, or the host application removed the place which the token designated. The surface is unmapped, the compositor ignores the requests on this object, and the client should destroy it.
